card.name: Words just before a verb phrase
card.fires_on: Mid-sentence words in general web prose, often a noun, auxiliary or relative word right before the verb or clause that follows (may, have, can, which, it). It appears in older or literary text, not in drug labels.

modes.label: Auxiliary or relative word
modes.description: A small word such as may, have, can, which or it that introduces the verb of a clause.
modes.example: Such of his early poems as<< have>> been preserved hardly contain the promise of what

modes.label: Noun inside a compound
modes.description: A noun that begins or continues a compound phrase, with the head noun still to come.
modes.example: She was referring to Britain’s strongly unionised<< coal>>-mining industry.

card.plain: It fires on ordinary connecting words in the middle of a sentence, right before the verb or the rest of the phrase arrives.
